subject: Vendor gateway onboarding — portal registration, MSA exceptions, and PO field mapping
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@biomed-supply.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medrx.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Portal access & initial MSA questions for onboarding

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. We want to move the Biomed Supply account into your procurement gateway (Coupa) next week. Before we kick off registration, a few items procurement asked me to confirm: 1) whether Redwood can accept the PO with a separate billing contact field (our ERP will send billing to billing@biomed-supply.com) and 2) a short list of MSA exceptions we flagged during the review (we'll attach the vendor redlines).

Quick background: our eProcurement team requires the portal to accept a free-text PO comment field and a custom order type code (up to 6 chars). If those aren't available we need to know how Redwood populates PO fields in outbound invoices. Also, procurement has a standard security addendum question about token retention — they requested a timeline and whether logs for token access are available for audit.

I've attached our redlines for the MSA and a preliminary PO mapping sheet. Can your team confirm whether these are supportable in the Coupa registration flow and if any contractual exceptions will block provisioning? Happy to hop on a quick call.

Attachments: MSA_redlines_Biomed_v1.docx (docx), PO_field_mapping_Biomed.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Sasha
Vendor Operations | Biomed Supply Co.
cell: +1 415-555-0192

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@biomed-supply.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portal access & initial MSA questions for onboarding

Thanks Sasha — this is helpful. Looping Dev (platform integrations) and Marissa (legal ops).

Quick answers up front:
- Billing contact: Coupa supports a separate billing contact. We'll confirm the vendor field name the portal expects (likely "InvoiceTo/BillTo contact").
- PO comment field: Coupa can accept a free-text PO comment; we do surface that back on the order->invoice mapping, but I want Dev to confirm how we map to our internal order form when we ingest the vendor's PO XML.
- Order type code: 6-char custom codes are usually fine; we'll validate the schema for our gateway.
- Token retention / audit logs: Marissa, can you confirm the standard language we provide for token retention and whether we can produce access logs on a per-vendor basis for audits?

Next steps: 1) Dev to validate PO XML element names and confirm whether any transformation is required, 2) Legal to flag any MSA redlines that are non-starters so we can decide if a short exception can be handled operationally, 3) I'll prepare a portal registration checklist and target a Coupa invite on Mon 10/5 if the scope is confirmed.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Vendor Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@biomed-supply.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portal access & initial MSA questions for onboarding

On Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 11:04 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers up front:
> - Billing contact: Coupa supports a separate billing contact. We'll confirm the vendor field name the portal expects (likely "InvoiceTo/BillTo contact").
> - PO comment field: Coupa can accept a free-text PO comment; we do surface that back on the order->invoice mapping, but I want Dev to confirm how we map to our internal order form when we ingest the vendor's PO XML.

Confirming: our gateway consumes the standard Coupa PO XML (cxml) which exposes the following elements we can map: OrderRequest/Order/OrderItems and Order/AdditionalInfo (free text). We currently map AdditionalInfo into order.notes and also pass order.notes into the invoice payload. For the billing contact we expect a contact element with role="bill-to"; if Biomed's ERP puts billing as an alternate contact tag we'll transform it on ingest but need a stable identifier (email or vendor_contact_id).

For order type code: we have an "order_type" custom attribute in our schema (string, max 8 chars) so 6 chars is fine.

I'll review the PO mapping sheet and reply with any transformation rules. If there are schema mismatches I can add a one-off transform for this vendor before the Coupa invite.

Dev
Senior Integrations Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: PO_field_mapping_Biomed.xlsx (uploaded to ticket)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@biomed-supply.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portal access & initial MSA questions for onboarding

Hi Sasha — thanks for sending the redlines. I took a pass and have flagged three items that likely require legal escalation:

1) Data residency / auditability: your redline asks for per-vendor audit log exports and a 24-month retention guarantee. Our standard position is to retain operational logs for 12 months; we can evaluate exporting vendor-specific logs on a case-by-case basis but would need a commercial addendum for extended retention.

2) Indemnity carveouts: the redline broadens indemnity to cover downstream third parties. That's a material change — Legal (Laura) recommends reverting to standard indemnity language or specifying a narrow carveout tied to Redwood-controlled code.

3) PO acceptance timing: you requested an explicit 72-hour acceptance window in the MSA. We typically accept POs upon fulfillment and rely on the Order Form to define service start dates. We can capture SLA expectations on the order form, not in the core MSA.

Operationally we can proceed with portal registration while legal reviews the redlines, but we need sign-off on whether Biomed will accept a standard retention term (12 months) or if procurement wants to route this to procurement/legal for a commercial amendment.

I'll attach my annotated redline doc and the portal onboarding checklist I propose (covers required fields, portal contact, mapping expectations).

Attachments: MSA_redlines_Biomed_v1_annotated.docx, portal_onboarding_checklist.pdf

- Marissa
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Portal access & initial MSA questions for onboarding

Thanks everyone — useful thread. Summary and next actions:

1) Portal provisioning: Dev will prepare a Coupa invite and a one-off transform if needed for Biomed's billing contact mapping. Targeting invite for Mon 10/05. (Dev to confirm by EOD Monday.)

2) Legal redlines: Marissa and Laura will review the annotated MSA and propose either (a) standard language with a commercial addendum for extended log retention, or (b) explicit carveouts tied to Redwood operations. Laura, can you provide an escalation note with suggested language by Tue 10/06?

3) PO mapping: Dev to deliver a short mapping appendix we can attach to the order form (to handle order_type and AdditionalInfo -> order.notes).

4) Procurement ask: Sasha, if Biomed can accept the 12-month retention while legal discusses a paid addendum, we can continue with portal setup and Coupa activation. Please confirm by Monday.

I'll upload the portal checklist to the shared drive and grant Biomed read access once legal confirms the path.

Attachments: portal_onboarding_checklist.pdf (uploaded)
Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/biomed-portal-checklist

Thanks — Olga
